description.@value: Guarantees stage 1 always has at least one matching rule so the pipeline proceeds to stage 2 regardless of whether any structural violation was found. Required because Graylog 7.1.9's 'stage match: either' halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all when ZERO rules in the current stage match -- confirmed empirically during PID-03 delivery: every genuinely clean, fully-conformant FalconEvent has every flag-check rule evaluate false, which silently stopped ALL valid traffic from ever reaching the routing stage until this rule was added.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - stage 1 passthrough"
when
    true
then
    set_field("falcon_stage1_evaluated", true);
end

description.@value: supersedes_event_id must never equal the event's own falcon_event_id -- an event cannot supersede itself.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag self-referential supersession"
when
    has_field("supersedes_event_id") &&
    has_field("falcon_event_id") &&
    to_string($message.supersedes_event_id) == to_string($message.falcon_event_id)
then
    set_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession", true);
end

description.@value: Any message flagged by stage-1 structural checks is routed to FALCON: Quarantine and removed from the default stream, and never reaches a trusted producer stream.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - route INVALID to Quarantine"
when
    (has_field("falcon_missing_required_field") && to_bool($message.falcon_missing_required_field)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unknown_producer_system") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_producer_system)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unknown_component") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_component)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unregistered_evidence_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_evidence_family)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_bad_timestamp") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_timestamp)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_decimal_type_violation") && to_bool($message.falcon_decimal_type_violation)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_causation_id_shape)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession") && to_bool($message.falcon_self_referential_supersession)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_unregistered_score_definition") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_score_definition)) ||
    (has_field("falcon_payload_field_outside_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_payload_field_outside_family))
then
    set_field("falcon_validity", "INVALID");
    route_to_stream(name: "FALCON: Quarantine", remove_from_default: true);
end

description.@value: Non-flagged tron.* events (excluding tron.health) route to FALCON: TRON evidence. See HERMES rule's description for why the invalid-condition is inlined and why this must share a stage with the quarantine rule.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - route valid TRON evidence"
when
    !(
        (has_field("falcon_missing_required_field") && to_bool($message.falcon_missing_required_field)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unknown_producer_system") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_producer_system)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unknown_component") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_component)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unregistered_evidence_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_evidence_family)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_bad_timestamp") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_timestamp)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_decimal_type_violation") && to_bool($message.falcon_decimal_type_violation)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_causation_id_shape)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession") && to_bool($message.falcon_self_referential_supersession)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unregistered_score_definition") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_score_definition)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_payload_field_outside_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_payload_field_outside_family))
    ) &&
    has_field("producer_system_id") &&
    to_string($message.producer_system_id) == "tron" &&
    (!has_field("evidence_family") || !ends_with(to_string($message.evidence_family), ".health"))
then
    set_field("falcon_validity", "VALID");
    route_to_stream(name: "FALCON: TRON evidence", remove_from_default: true);
end

description.@value: FALCON-owned ingestion timestamp: always overwritten by Graylog at pipeline time, never taken from producer input, per FALCON-UNIVERSAL-EVENT-CONTRACT.md.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - Set falcon_ingested_at_utc"
when
    true
then
    set_field("falcon_ingested_at_utc", format_date(now("UTC"), "yyyy-MM-dd'T'HH:mm:ss.SSS'Z'", "UTC"));
end

description.@value: Structural check: flags a message missing any of the envelope's core identity/routing/integrity fields.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag missing required fields"
when
    !has_field("falcon_event_id") ||
    !has_field("producer_system_id") ||
    !has_field("evidence_family") ||
    !has_field("evidence_type") ||
    !has_field("produced_at_utc") ||
    !has_field("payload_hash")
then
    set_field("falcon_missing_required_field", true);
end

description.@value: payload_score_definition_id, when present, must be a registered score definition. Only helios.entry_confidence.v1 is registered in this PID's tested scope -- any other value is flagged. Narrow/non-exhaustive by design; see PID-03 evidence notes.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag unregistered score definition"
when
    has_field("payload_score_definition_id") &&
    to_string($message.payload_score_definition_id) != "helios.entry_confidence.v1"
then
    set_field("falcon_unregistered_score_definition", true);
end

description.@value: PID-03 canonical FALCON ingestion pipeline. Stage 0 un-flattens JSON sub-objects and sets the FALCON-owned ingestion timestamp (always has a match via its own always-true/has_field rules). Stage 1 runs native structural validation checks against stage-0-derived payload_* fields, plus a dedicated always-true passthrough rule -- required because Graylog 7.1.9 halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all when a stage has ZERO matching rules under 'match either', and every genuinely clean FalconEvent makes every flag-check rule evaluate false. Stage 2 routes every message to FALCON: Quarantine OR its trusted per-producer stream, in ONE stage, using a fully self-contained (inlined) invalid-condition per rule rather than a shared derived field, because rules within one stage do not see each other's field mutations (only rules in a later stage do) -- both mechanics were confirmed empirically during PID-03 delivery and are documented in the PID-03 delivery report.

source.@value:
pipeline "FALCON Ingestion"
stage 0 match either
    rule "FALCON - Parse payload JSON"
    rule "FALCON - Parse provenance_ref JSON"
    rule "FALCON - Set falcon_ingested_at_utc"
stage 1 match either
    rule "FALCON - stage 1 passthrough"
    rule "FALCON - flag missing required fields"
    rule "FALCON - flag unknown producer system"
    rule "FALCON - flag unknown component"
    rule "FALCON - flag unregistered evidence family"
    rule "FALCON - flag non-UTC or naive timestamp"
    rule "FALCON - flag decimal type violation"
    rule "FALCON - flag malformed causation_id shape"
    rule "FALCON - flag self-referential supersession"
    rule "FALCON - flag unregistered score definition"
    rule "FALCON - flag hermes payload carrying TRON-scoped field"
stage 2 match either
    rule "FALCON - route INVALID to Quarantine"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HERMES evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid ARES evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HELIOS Trade Suggestions"
    rule "FALCON - route valid HELIOS evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid TRON evidence"
    rule "FALCON - route valid Operational Health evidence"
end

title.@value: FALCON - flag hermes payload carrying TRON-scoped field

description.@value: Targeted, known cross-family field-scope violation: broker_order_id is registered only for TRON order families, never for hermes.market_fact. This is a specific authored check, not a generalised additionalProperties/field-registry-scope validator (Graylog 7.1.9 pipeline rules cannot enumerate arbitrary map keys -- see PID-03 evidence notes on the unknown_field negative class).

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag hermes payload carrying TRON-scoped field"
when
    has_field("evidence_family") &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) == "hermes.market_fact" &&
    has_field("payload_broker_order_id")
then
    set_field("falcon_payload_field_outside_family", true);
end

description.@value: producer_system_id must be one of the registered system IDs (registry/system_component_registry.v1.json).

    to_string($message.producer_system_id) != "neo"

    set_field("falcon_unknown_producer_system", true);
end

description.@value: Un-flattens the payload_json GELF field (JSON-encoded FalconEvent typed payload) into individual payload_* fields, preserving JSON scalar types (decimal-string values stay strings; numeric mirrors stay numbers).

when

then

end

description.@value: Non-flagged hermes.* events (excluding hermes.health) route to FALCON: HERMES evidence. The 'not invalid' condition is inlined (not read from a sibling rule's derived falcon_validity field) because Graylog 7.1.9 pipeline rules within the SAME stage do not see each other's field mutations -- confirmed empirically during PID-03 delivery. This also fixes a second, more serious bug: putting the quarantine rule alone in its own stage meant that stage had zero matching rules for any clean valid message, and a stage with zero matches under 'match either' halts the pipeline before the next stage runs at all -- so no valid message was EVER reaching a trusted stream under that structure. Quarantine and valid-routing must therefore be evaluated together, in one stage, each with a complete self-contained condition.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - route valid HERMES evidence"
when
    !(
        (has_field("falcon_missing_required_field") && to_bool($message.falcon_missing_required_field)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unknown_producer_system") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_producer_system)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unknown_component") && to_bool($message.falcon_unknown_component)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unregistered_evidence_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_evidence_family)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_bad_timestamp") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_timestamp)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_decimal_type_violation") && to_bool($message.falcon_decimal_type_violation)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape") && to_bool($message.falcon_bad_causation_id_shape)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_self_referential_supersession") && to_bool($message.falcon_self_referential_supersession)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_unregistered_score_definition") && to_bool($message.falcon_unregistered_score_definition)) ||
        (has_field("falcon_payload_field_outside_family") && to_bool($message.falcon_payload_field_outside_family))

end

rule "FALCON - flag decimal type violation"
when
    (has_field("payload_value_decimal") && !is_string($message.payload_value_decimal)) ||
    (has_field("payload_reference_price_decimal") && !is_string($message.payload_reference_price_decimal)) ||

description.@value: causation_id, when present, must reference exactly one causing event (a falcon_event_id UUID shape: 8-4-4-4-12 hex with dashes at fixed positions, 36 chars total) -- not a broad correlation-style label. Catches causation_id/correlation_id semantic confusion. Implemented via length()/substring() dash-position checks rather than regex().matches, which this Graylog 7.1.9 pipeline rule grammar rejects (RequestError: 'Expected type Boolean but found Object' when chaining .matches off a function call in a when clause -- confirmed empirically).

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag malformed causation_id shape"
when
    has_field("causation_id") &&
    (
        length(to_string($message.causation_id)) != 36 ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 8, 9) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 13, 14) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 18, 19) != "-" ||
        substring(to_string($message.causation_id), 23, 24) != "-"
    )
then
    set_field("falcon_bad_causation_id_shape", true);
end

title.@value: FALCON - flag non-UTC or naive timestamp

description.@value: produced_at_utc must be timezone-aware AND UTC (suffix Z or +00:00) -- naive datetimes and non-UTC offsets are both rejected per the temporal law.

source.@value:
rule "FALCON - flag non-UTC or naive timestamp"
when
    has_field("produced_at_utc") &&
    !ends_with(to_string($message.produced_at_utc), "Z") &&
    !ends_with(to_string($message.produced_at_utc), "+00:00")
then
    set_field("falcon_bad_timestamp", true);
end

    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.fill" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.position_state" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.protection_state" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.exit" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.trade_outcome" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.execution_quality" &&
    to_string($message.evidence_family) != "tron.health"
then
    set_field("falcon_unregistered_evidence_family", true);
end
